subject: VPC demarcation handoff: control-plane / data-plane runbook and ops ownership
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, ops@acme-corp.com
Cc: d.smith@edgecloud.io
Date: Thu, 02 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial handoff: private VPC demarcation & runbook

Hi team,

Attaching the demarcation diagram and a draft ops runbook for the Acme private VPC. This is the baseline we discussed in the architecture sync. Key points in the draft: 

- Control plane: customer-managed control-plane components are in the customer VPC (separate control-plane subnet). Control plane initiates no inbound connections to the inference subnets; it registers agents via mTLS.
- Data plane: inference nodes live in an isolated subnet with a strict egress policy. All outbound traffic must transit the egress appliance in the edge VLAN. No public IPs on inference hosts.
- Telemetry: OTLP/Prom push over an allowlisted egress path; metrics endpoint reachable only from our ingestion proxies.

Open questions called out in the runbook (see section "Decisions required"):
1) Will Acme host the egress appliance (preferred) or accept our shared edge appliance?
2) Can Acme provide a routable /28 for control-plane management IPs or do we need a NAT bounce?
3) Certificate rotation cadence for mTLS between agents and control plane (recommended 90 days).

Attachments: 
- vpc-demarc-diagram-v2.drawio.png (diagram)
- private-vpc-runbook-v1.md (draft runbook)

Requesting: Acme ops to confirm hosting model and IP allocation. Internal owners: please call out any non-starter items so I can fold into the runbook before handoff.

Thanks,

Irene Choi
Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_chooi@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 02 Apr 2026 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial handoff: private VPC demarcation & runbook

Thanks Irene — useful start. A few quick items from GTM/CS perspective that need explicit language in the runbook before I present to the Acme procurement lead:

- Clear ownership matrix: which team owns certificate rotation, who triages agent disconnects, and who opens firewall change requests.
- Escalation path / SLOs: what constitutes a Sev-1 vs Sev-2 for the control-plane connectivity?
- Billing implication note if customer hosts egress appliance (we expect a $X/mo ops surcharge).

Irene: can you add a one-page "handoff checklist" at the top of the runbook so I can pass it to Acme ops? Also let's lock a 30-min sync today to walk the diagram live. Rafael/Aditya: Rafael, please confirm the NAT vs route decision and whether the control-plane can operate behind a customer NAT without feature loss.

I'll book 11:30 PT if that works for everyone.

Best,

Kimberly Park
Senior Manager, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Initial handoff: private VPC demarcation & runbook -- technical notes

Kimberly / Irene / Acme ops team,

Short technical clarifications after reviewing the diagram:

- NAT vs routed control-plane: Control-plane behind a symmetric NAT will work for agent registration and heartbeats if we use outbound-initiated mTLS with long-lived connection (we maintain the connection to the control-plane). However, features that require inbound callbacks (e.g., on-demand debug sessions that rely on a reverse shell) will need a stable inbound path or a relay. If Acme cannot provide a routable range, we'll implement a relay service in the shared edge (extra latency for debug flows).
- Egress appliance: Recommend host the egress appliance in the edge VLAN with an S2S route to the inference subnet. Appliance sizing: for Acme's 100 QPS steady-state and 1.5 TB/day peaks, we recommend 2 vCPU / 8GB and 500 Mbps NIC with CPU offload.
- Security: mutual TLS for agent-control plane; we propose ACME's PKI issue leaf certs and Redwood rotates control-plane certs. Need an API for cert enrollment (SCEP/ACME) — call this out in the runbook.

I've attached a short Acme ops note with the appliance sizing and NAT behavior. Also added inline comments on the drawio for route tables and subnet ACLs.

Attachments:
- ops-handbook-acme-note.pdf
- (updated) vpc-demarc-diagram-v3.drawio.png (inline comments)

If Acme confirms they will host the appliance, we can remove the relay plan and simplify the runbook.

Rafael
Senior Network Engineer
Redwood Inference

Hi all,

Acme ops reviewed the diagram and the sizing note. We can host the egress appliance in our edge VLAN. Confirming:

- We will provide a /28 for control-plane management; no inbound public IPs on inference hosts.
- Appliance will be in a dedicated HA pair; sizing looks reasonable. Networking team will open the S2S route to the inference subnet.
- For certificates: we can stand up a SCEP endpoint to issue agent leaf certs; will coordinate rotation cadence (90 days acceptable).

Next steps:
1) Kimberly/Irene: please share the final one-page handoff checklist and updated runbook after you fold Rafael's notes in.
2) Rafael: please add the relay plan as an appendix (we may keep it as an emergency fallback).
3) Schedule the 11:30 PT sync — we will be on the call.

Thanks,
